verificationTemplate:
VERIFICATION

I, {plaintiff_name}, son/daughter/wife of {plaintiff_father_name}, aged about {plaintiff_age} years, resident of {plaintiff_address}, do hereby verify that the contents of paragraphs 1 to {lastParagraph} of the above plaint are true and correct to my personal knowledge, and matters of legal submission are believed true on advice of counsel. No part is false and nothing material has been concealed.

Verified at {place} on this {date}.

Plaintiff

promptInstructions: Draft a plaint for recovery of money strictly in accordance with Order VII CPC (Rules 1 to 9) and Order VI (general pleading rules).
Para 1: Describe the Plaintiff with full particulars per Order VII R.1(a).
Para 2: Describe the Defendant per Order VII R.1(b).
Para 3 onwards: State the transaction giving rise to the claim — basis (loan / PN / cheque / account stated / goods sold / services rendered), date, place, consideration, mode.
Plead documentary basis with particulars — date of execution, parties, witnesses, where document is in possession of Plaintiff (Order VII R.14).
Where based on a promissory note, ensure it is duly stamped and recite stamping particulars; an unstamped PN is inadmissible (Indian Stamp Act).
Where based on a dishonoured cheque, plead the cheque particulars, dishonour memo, demand notice, and reservation of S.138 NI Act remedy (these are separate proceedings).
Plead defendant's failure to pay despite demand / legal notice.

Para on Cause of Action — Order VII R.1(e) requires specific statement of when and where cause of action accrued. State all relevant dates: date of advance, date of demand, date of refusal, date of legal notice.

Para on Limitation — Order VII R.6 requires specific pleading of grounds of exemption if suit is filed beyond ordinary limitation. Cite specific Article (e.g., Article 19 for money lent — 3 years from when loan made; Article 34 for PN payable on demand — 3 years from date of PN).

Para on Jurisdiction — Order VII R.1(f). Territorial jurisdiction under S.20 CPC (defendant resides / carries on business / cause of action wholly or in part arose). Pecuniary jurisdiction per state-specific notification.

If suit value exceeds Rs. 3 lakh and dispute is 'commercial' u/s 2(1)(c) Commercial Courts Act 2015, file before Commercial Court / Commercial Division. Pre-institution mediation u/s 12A CCA is mandatory unless urgent interim relief sought (Patil Automation v. Rakheja Engineers (2022) — mandatory).
Para on Valuation and Court Fee — Order VII R.1(i)(j). Valuation must equal the amount claimed. Court fee per state Schedule (e.g., Court Fees Act 1870 + state amendments).

Para on Relief — Order VII R.7. Specifically claim: (i) principal sum; (ii) interest up to date of suit (cite agreement/PN or S.80 NI Act for cheque); (iii) pendente lite and future interest u/s 34 CPC; (iv) costs.
Tone: precise, fact-based. Avoid argumentative tone — plead facts, not law.
Verification: Order VI R.15 — verify which paragraphs are on personal knowledge and which on information/legal advice.
Affidavit in support: Order VI R.15(4) post-2002 amendment — mandatory affidavit verifying plaint.
List of documents (Order VII R.14) and list of witnesses (Order XVI R.1) must accompany the plaint.

filing_checklist: Plaint (original + copies as per court rules)
Affidavit in support of plaint (Order VI R.15(4))
Court fee — ad valorem on suit amount (state Schedule)
Statement of truth (in Commercial Courts — Order VI R.15A)
List of documents (Order VII R.14) with index
Original documents — loan agreement / promissory note (duly stamped) / cheque / dishonour memo
Copy of legal notice and postal receipts / track consignment
Pre-institution mediation non-starter certificate (if commercial, when applicable)
Disclaimer slip — Lawie drafting assistance acknowledged
validation_rules: plaintiff_name and defendant_name must not be empty
limitation_start_date must be within 3 years of filing for ordinary money claims
If total_suit_amount >= 300000 and commercial_dispute=true, flag for Commercial Court track
If commercial_dispute=true and no urgent interim relief, pre_institution_mediation must be true (Patil Automation)
advocate_enrollment must match Bar Council format
key_citations: Patil Automation Pvt Ltd v. Rakheja Engineers Pvt Ltd (2022) SCC OnLine SC 1028 — Pre-institution mediation u/s 12A CCA is mandatory
Dhulabhai v. State of M.P. (1968) 3 SCR 662 — Jurisdiction of civil courts
Liverpool & London S.P. & I Association v. M.V. Sea Success I (2004) 9 SCC 512 — Order VII R.11 rejection scope
Saleem Bhai v. State of Maharashtra (2003) 1 SCC 557 — Plaint must disclose cause of action
T. Arivandandam v. T.V. Satyapal (1977) 4 SCC 467 — Manifestly vexatious plaints may be rejected
Kandimalla Raghavaiah v. National Insurance Co (2009) 7 SCC 768 — Limitation cannot be extended by acknowledgement after period expires
